title: Privacy
summary: Wild Neighbors works at the level of a neighborhood, never you. There are no accounts, no ads, no analytics and no tracking.

sections.heading: Your location
sections.body: If you choose to use your location, the app asks your phone once, at low accuracy, and turns your position into a neighborhood cell, an area about 1.2 by 0.6 kilometers, right on your phone. Your exact location is never stored and never leaves your phone. You can also pick a neighborhood from the list instead.

sections.heading: What leaves your phone
sections.body: Only one thing: to get the weather, the app sends Open-Meteo the center of your neighborhood cell, rounded to about a kilometer. No account, device ID or cookies go with it. Open-Meteo's own privacy policy covers their service.

sections.heading: What stays on your phone
sections.body: Your saved neighborhoods, your kindness checkmarks for the season, your sound and morning-note settings, and a cache of recent sightings. Deleting the app deletes all of it. The photos, sounds and stories are built into the app, so looking at them doesn't send anything anywhere.

sections.heading: The morning note
sections.body: The daily note is off until you turn it on. It's scheduled on your phone, a week at a time, and no push service or server is involved.

sections.heading: The animals' privacy, too
sections.body: The app is about species, never individual animals. It never shows where any animal is: it talks about neighborhoods, parks and blocks, not spots.

sections.heading: What we don't do
sections.body: No accounts. No ads. No analytics or tracking. We don't sell or share data, because we don't collect any about you. Wild Neighbors doesn't collect personal information from anyone, including children.

sections.heading: Changes and questions
sections.body: If this policy changes, the new version will be in the app with a new date. Questions? Write to {contact}.
